skill.name: mirrord-chaos
skill.description: Help users chaos test their app with mirrord: inject artificial latency or connection errors into a mirrord session's outgoing traffic via per-session chaos rules managed with the `mirrord chaos` CLI. Use when a user wants to add latency or delay to outgoing connections or a dependency (e.g. a slow database), simulate connection failures (reset, timed out, refused), test app behavior under degraded network conditions, or wire chaos rules into CI test runs. Always use this skill instead of the deprecated _experimental_.latency mirrord config option.
skill.summary: Create and manage session-scoped mirrord chaos rules for latency and connection-failure testing in interactive and CI workflows.
skill.author: metalbear-co

security_audit.summary: All 78 static findings are false positives for this document-only skill. The flagged commands are explicit mirrord, shell, and text-processing examples for session-scoped chaos testing; no malicious installation, credential access, exfiltration, or prompt injection was found.

remediation.issue: Chaos commands can affect real dependencies when a mirrord session targets production.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the existing staging-only warning prominent and require an explicit production approval process before applying rules.

remediation.issue: The CI example extracts a session identifier with shell pipelines.
remediation.suggestion: Use a trusted, pinned mirrord runner and validate the extracted session identifier before applying or deleting rules.

remediation.issue: The guide includes a command that deletes all chaos rules for a session.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer deleting by rule ID when possible and require a deliberate cleanup step for the session-wide delete command.

content.value_statement: Teams need realistic failure tests without changing shared workloads or application code. This skill creates session-scoped mirrord rules for latency and connection failures in local and CI tests.
actual_capabilities: Create valid mirrord chaos rule files for latency and connection errors.
Explain session scope, selectors, percentages, priorities, and hit counts.
Provide commands to add, list, edit, and delete session rules.
Design CI workflows that apply reviewed rules and clean them up.
Troubleshoot validation errors, missing sessions, and rules that do not fire.
limitations: Chaos rules currently target outgoing TCP connections only.
The chaos feature requires a compatible mirrord CLI and a live session.
The feature is alpha and may change between mirrord releases.
The skill does not install mirrord or verify a production environment.

use_cases.title: Test Retry Behavior
use_cases.description: Inject timeouts or refused connections into selected dependency traffic and verify application retries, fallbacks, and error handling.

use_cases.title: Add Failure Scenarios to CI
use_cases.description: Version rule files with integration tests, apply them to a tagged mirrord session, and remove them after the test run.

use_cases.title: Investigate Rule Behavior
use_cases.description: Inspect active rules, priorities, percentages, identifiers, and hit counts when a chaos scenario behaves unexpectedly.

prompt_templates.title: Add Basic Latency
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a mirrord chaos rule that adds read latency to 25 percent of outgoing TCP connections to my database host. Explain each field.

prompt_templates.title: Simulate a Timeout
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to make calls to payments.internal time out in a live mirrord session, then provide the cleanup command.

prompt_templates.title: Build a CI Scenario
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a CI workflow that starts a tagged mirrord session, finds its session ID, applies reviewed chaos rules, runs integration tests, and always cleans up.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve Rule Conflicts
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these mirrord chaos rules and explain which rule wins for each matching upstream. Identify invalid effects, priorities, percentages, and selectors.

output_examples.input: Make 30 percent of payments API calls time out.
output_examples.output: A session-scoped timeout rule targeting the payments API, plus commands to apply it and remove it after testing.

output_examples.input: Why does my latency rule never fire?
output: Check that the session is active and the upstream uses an outgoing TCP connection.
Confirm that the rule has a nonzero read or write delay and that its percentage is valid.
Inspect the rule identifier and hit count after generating test traffic.

best_practices: Run chaos tests against staging dependencies whenever possible.
Review rule files with the tests that use them.
Include deterministic cleanup in every CI workflow.
anti_patterns: Do not use deprecated experimental latency configuration for new scenarios.
Do not apply broad failure rules to production sessions without approval.
Do not depend on rule names when identifiers are available.

faq.question: What does this skill control?
faq.answer: It controls chaos rules attached to one mirrord session and its outgoing traffic.

faq.question: Which traffic can rules match?
faq.answer: Current selectors match outgoing TCP connections. File and HTTP selectors are not active.

faq.question: Which effects are supported?
faq.answer: The guide covers read or write latency and reset, timed-out, or refused connection errors.

faq.question: What version do I need?
faq.answer: Use a mirrord CLI version that supports the chaos command, currently 3.241.0 or newer.

faq.question: Can I use this in CI?
faq.answer: Yes. Store reviewed rule files, identify a tagged session, apply the rules, and clean them up after testing.

faq.question: Does this change the cluster workload?
faq.answer: No. Rules affect the outgoing traffic of the mirrord session, but production dependencies can still receive real requests.
